\[
N = 255 - Y,
\quad
B = G_\sigma * N,
\quad
S = 255 \cdot \begin{cases} 0 & Y = 0 \\ 1 & B = 255 \\ \min\left(1, \dfrac{Y / 255}{1 - B / 255}\right) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases},
\qquad \sigma = 8
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(Y\): The luma 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B
- \(N, B\): The negative and the blurred negative
- \(S\): The sketch

Y is the luma, N its negative and B the negative blurred with a Gaussian cut at 3 sigma. S is the color dodge of the W3C Compositing and Blending spec, with Y as the backdrop and B as the source. In flat areas B is close to N, so Y / (1 - B / 255) is close to 1 and the area turns white. Near an edge the blur mixes in the other side, so the dodge stays below 1 and leaves a gray line. The recipe of dodging with a blurred negative is PixelNexus's own choice, though photo editors use the same idea. With Keep colors on, the color differences C - Y of the image are added back to S.
